cards.text: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus, is writing to the saints in Ephesus (Ephesians 1:1), and he's just written that in all things we will grow up into Christ Himself (Ephesians 4:15). Now he gets serious. He insists in the Lord that they must no longer walk as the Gentiles do, in the futility of their thinking.
Paul says their understanding is darkened, and they're alienated from the life of God. Friend, I lived in the back of a junk drawer for YEARS, so believe me, dark is no way to live.

cards.question: Paul says the Gentiles are alienated from the life of God because of the ignorance in them. What is that ignorance due to?

cards.text: And Paul keeps going. Having lost all sense of shame, they've given themselves over to sensuality, for the practice of every kind of impurity.

cards.question: Paul says they've given themselves over to practice every kind of impurity. What else does he say they have?

cards.text: A craving for more. It's the snooze button, friend: in all of history, NOBODY has ever hit it just once.

cards.question: Then Paul turns to the believers. True or false: he says this way of living is not the way they came to know Christ.
Paul says the believers heard of Christ and were taught in Him. What was that teaching in keeping with?

answers.text: The truth that is in Jesus

cards.text: Then Paul spells out what they were taught, and it comes in three steps, like a recipe card. And I LOVE a short recipe card, friend, because the long ones always end with me covered in flour.

cards.question: Step one: put off their former way of life. What does Paul call that former way of life?
True or false: Paul says the old self is being corrupted by its deceitful desires.

cards.text: So you put it OFF, like a stained old work shirt. Not "I'll patch it," not "one more season," just OFF.

cards.question: Step two: Paul says they were taught to be renewed in the spirit of their ___.

cards.text: Step three, and here's the good part: put on the new self.

cards.question: Paul says the new self is created to be like ___ in true righteousness and holiness.

cards.text: True righteousness and holiness. Friend, when God made me new, my edges came out so SHARP I'm scared to hug myself.
Now Paul gets practical, starting with the mouth. Each of them must put off falsehood and speak truthfully to his neighbor.

cards.question: Why does Paul say each believer must speak truthfully to his neighbor?

answers.text: We are all members of one another
We will all stand before the Lord
Our words are weighed by God

cards.text: Lying to your neighbor is like your left hand lying to your right hand about who ate the last cookie. Friend, you share a STOMACH.
Next up, anger. Paul quotes a short line about it, and the line has two parts.

cards.question: Paul quotes a short line about anger. True or false: the line says being angry is always a sin.
Paul's line is "Be angry, yet do not sin." Then he puts a deadline on anger. What is it?

answers.text: Don't let the sun set on it

cards.text: Sundown, friend. Your anger works the DAY shift only: no overtime, no night shift, CLOCK OUT.

cards.question: Paul adds one more warning about anger: do not give the ___ a foothold.

cards.text: Then Paul speaks to anyone who has been stealing. He must steal no longer, and must work, doing good with his own hands.

cards.question: Paul gives the former thief a reason to work with his own hands. What is it?

answers.text: To have something to share with the one in need
To pay back everyone he ever stole from
To earn back his good name around town

cards.text: From swiping stuff to running the coat drive. Friend, that is a CAREER change.

cards.question: Paul's back to the mouth: let no unwholesome talk come out of it. What kind of talk should come out instead?

answers.text: Only what builds up the one in need
Only what shows how much you know

cards.question: True or false: Paul says helpful talk brings grace to those who listen.
Paul says do not grieve the Holy Spirit of God. True or false: he says they were sealed in the Spirit for the day of redemption.

cards.text: Sealed for a day, friend, and sealing boxes for a big day is my WHOLE job. I've sealed so many boxes I once sealed my own mustache in one, TWICE in the same week.
Then Paul clears the counter. Bitterness, rage, anger, outcry, slander and every form of malice: get rid of ALL of it.

cards.question: Last line. Paul says be kind and tenderhearted to one another. How should they forgive each other?

answers.text: Just as in Christ God forgave them
As each one confesses his sin
Seven times and then no more

cards.text: God pulled me out of a junk drawer, friend. So I am NOT starting a new drawer full of grudges.

findings.problem: Several choice questions rely on context that is no longer on screen. In stop 1, cards 5, 10 and 13 use 'they' or 'their' without identifying the Gentiles or believers, and card 7 refers to 'this way of living' without identifying the Gentiles' way of life. In stop 2, cards 14 and 17 likewise use 'they' without naming Paul's audience. Each question should supply its own antecedents and context.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: "Sealed for a day" changes Ephesians 4:30's "sealed for the day of redemption." The verse names the day of redemption; it does not describe a one-day duration. The joke's setup should preserve that meaning.

rule.text: Retelling: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: This story card is only Papa Dorin's personal joke about not keeping a drawer of grudges. It does not tell any part of Ephesians 4:32, the verse it cites, or carry the passage forward; the kindness, tenderheartedness and Christ-patterned forgiveness appear only in the preceding choice card.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.
